problem: Existing MLLM benchmarks use static images/videos and are non-interactive, while existing embodied benchmarks are task-specific, template-based, low in scene diversity, use rigid I/O formats (e.g. 3D points) or text-only state, so they cannot comprehensively evaluate MLLMs as embodied agents.
motivation: MLLMs are increasingly used as embodied agents needing egocentric perception, grounding, spatial reasoning and memory, but there is no unified interactive benchmark to measure these in diverse scenes. The paper builds one with a unified vision-only input and discrete option-based output so any MLLM can be evaluated directly.
key_idea: EmbodiedEval is a benchmark of 328 diverse tasks across 125 scenes covering navigation, object interaction, social interaction, and attribute/spatial QA, in a unified interactive simulator with egocentric visual input and discrete option-based actions.
insight: Current MLLMs fall far short of humans (best GPT-4o 25.00% vs. human 97.26% success). Failures concentrate on spatial QA, interaction and long-horizon tasks: success drops as required steps increase, and giving Gemini-Flash more history images lowers performance except on spatial QA. Interaction analysis shows models have low interaction success (~9-11%) despite varying frequencies, indicating weak affordance judgment. Error analysis identifies grounding hallucination, insufficient exploration, poor spatial reasoning and wrong planning.
method: Evaluation loop: an MLLM receives task text, option list, egocentric image history and action history, picks an option each step, and the LEGENT simulator returns a new observation plus feedback; max 24 steps.
Unified I/O space: input is only text and first-person RGB images (448x448, 90° FOV) or video, with no extra state info; output is a selected option from movement, interaction, or answering.
Movement space: a pre-built per-scene navigation graph with move forward, turn left/right, look up/down actions, with density adapted to scene and task.

Interaction and answering space: open-vocabulary high-level interaction actions with preconditions (e.g. hand over requires holding an object near a person), plus distractor actions; QA uses 8 annotated options with strong distractors.

Predicate-based success: predicates (choose, agent_at, agent_pass, at, grab_once, grab, special_action_success) map sim state to boolean; a task succeeds when all hold; GcS measures the fraction satisfied.
Scene collection: 125 scenes from Objaverse (procedurally generated with GPT-3.5 annotations, manually edited), AI2THOR, HSSD, and Sketchfab.

Task collection and annotation: seed tasks from 30+ datasets expanded by Claude/ChatGPT, 300+ selected; 8 expert annotators using a Unity annotation tool, 3 reviewers per task, expert demos and non-expert human validation.

setting.backbone: 19 MLLMs evaluated (frozen): GPT-4o, GPT-4o-Mini, Gemini-1.5-Pro/Flash, Qwen-VL-Max, InternVL2, LLaVA-OneVision, LLaVA-NeXT, VILA, LLaVA-Video, Oryx, VideoLLaMA2; plus Random and Human agents
setting.training_data: none (benchmark; models evaluated zero-shot with a ReAct-style thought-then-choice prompt)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB images (448x448, 90° FOV) with observation history, or video for video MLLMs; no state info
setting.action_space: discrete options: nav-graph move forward / turn left-right / look up-down, open-vocabulary high-level interactions, and choosing among 8 textual answers

numbers.extra: max 24 steps, temperature 0, multi-image history input

numbers_note: Benchmark paper; the table reports results on its own benchmark (no official split names, so 'test' is used). The paper mentions 328 tasks but the Limitations mention 327 test cases. Other models' results are in Table 2 and are not repeated here.
results: Best model GPT-4o reaches only 25.00% success and 32.42% GcS versus 97.26% for non-expert humans; Random gets 5.49%. Best open-source model is LLaVA-OneVision-72B at 12.80%. Performance drops sharply on spatial QA, interaction (GPT-4o 10.11% object interaction) and long-horizon tasks.
limitations: Small evaluation set (328 tasks, the Limitations section says 327) due to costly manual verification
Movement and interaction are discretized (nav graph, high-level actions), so low-level control is not evaluated
Only one simulator (LEGENT) and greedy temperature 0 evaluation, which the authors note slightly underperforms temperature 1
